card.title: Grammar for Writing — sentences, clauses, punctuation

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: **Sentence types as tools:** simple (one clause — POWER), compound (two main clauses via and/but/so or a semicolon — equal weight), complex (main + subordinate clause via because/although/when/if — shows the relation between ideas). Mix them: examiners reward rhythm.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Trick 1: Clause ID: independent = complete thought; dependent = starts with subordinator (because, although, when); relative = who/which/that + verb — classify before combining.
Trick 2: Comma rules that pay: after introductory phrases, around non-essential clauses, before coordinating conjunctions joining two full clauses; semicolon joins two related full sentences.

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Tense + agreement discipline:** pick a tense zone per paragraph (essays: present; reports: past); subjects agree with verbs ('Each of the students WAS present'); a/an by SOUND ('an hour', 'a university').  ·  **Full guide:** Full model answers, starting-line banks and exam tips: [/knowledge/writing](/knowledge/writing).

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: **Clause types and punctuation duties (classified)** | Item | Definition | Punctuation rule | Example | |---|---|---|---| | Independent clause | Stands alone | Ends with . ? ! | She left early. | | Dependent clause | Cannot stand alone | Comma when first | When she left, we ate. | | Relative clause | Which/who/that | Commas if extra info | Ram, who runs, won.…  ·  **Punctuation quick map** | Mark | Job | Common misuse | |---|---|---| | Semicolon | Joins related clauses | Before a fragment | | Colon | Introduces list/explanation | After a verb directly | | Dash | Emphasis, aside | Overuse everywhere | | Apostrophe | Possession/contraction | Its vs it’s |

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Q. Identify the clause type: 'Although it rained, we played.' (1 mark) — dependent adverbial clause + independent clause (complex sentence).

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: **Clauses vs phrases:** a phrase has no subject-verb pair and cannot stand alone; a dependent clause has one but leans on the main clause ('Because it rained.' alone is a fragment). Relative clauses (who/which/that) add noun detail — commas only for extra information.  ·  **Punctuation logic:** full stop ends a thought; comma separates list items, follows openers, precedes and/but/so between full sentences; semicolon joins balanced sentences; colon introduces; apostrophe = possession or contraction (its vs it's is the classic trap). Comma splice = two full sentences joined by only a comma — fix it.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Trick 3: Sentence variety for writing marks: mix a simple, a compound and a complex sentence in every paragraph — uniform simple sentences cap the style band.  ·  Trick 4: Fragment test: read the sentence aloud alone — if it leaves a question hanging ('because he was late'), it is a fragment.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: Q. Fix the fragment: 'Because he was tired.' (1 mark) — attach an independent clause: 'Because he was tired, he slept early.'

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: **Tense + agreement discipline:** pick a tense zone per paragraph (essays: present; reports: past); subjects agree with verbs ('Each of the students WAS present'); a/an by SOUND ('an hour', 'a university').
